title: Micetro MCP Server for AI Assistants

cta.text: Connect your AI assistant to Micetro

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Micetro MCP Server for AI Assistants".
Start with one welcome step whose title is exactly "Let an AI Assistant Investigate DNS and DHCP" and whose text is exactly: Connect an AI assistant to live Micetro data via MCP, ask it why clients cannot get out and which nameserver is stale, see exactly how it found the answer, and see why the server is read-only by design: your operators stay in control.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
8 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element. Use the text of each numbered tooltip EXACTLY as written; do not rewrite, shorten or merge it. Do not add a closing step or a closing message after the last screenshot; its own tooltip is the end.
1. This is how Micetro shows a DHCP scope and its options in the UI. For troubleshooting, an AI assistant can often get to the root cause faster. Let's see how it reads this same data.
2. The MCP server runs as a small container next to Micetro. This health check shows it is up and signed in to Micetro.
3. Any assistant that supports MCP connects the same way. Here it can see Micetro's tools, and every one of them is read-only.
4. Now ask it the kind of question your team would ask. It looks at the scope and spots that the default gateway is on a different subnet.
5. This is the tool call it made to Micetro, so you can see where the answer came from.
6. Same setup, different question. It finds a nameserver that no longer resolves and confirms AppBIND still answers.
7. You can confirm it in Micetro. The zone has the same two nameservers.
8. Ask it to make the change and it sends you back to Micetro. The MCP server is read-only by design, so changes stay with your operators. Live answers from Micetro, with the working shown. Read-only by design, so your operators stay in control.
